body:
- **Slug:** stub-split-reaches-tracker
- **Defect / goal:** With `[leaves.splitter] mode = "stub"`, `pdca split <id> --accept`
  files the offline placeholder proposal as **real tracker sub-issues** and materialises
  child bundles from fixture text. Observed live: `getwyrd/wyrd#708` and `#709` are open
  right now as sub-issues of `#682`, titled literally **"stub-child-one"** and
  **"stub-child-two"**, and `results/issue_708/brief.md` / `issue_709/brief.md` carry the
  fixture body — nothing to do with 682's actual work. The children then derive as
  `PLANNED`, so `pdca flow 708` skipped the Plan beat and started at Do on a brief no model
  ever wrote.

  Nothing in the chain can tell a stub proposal from a real one:

  - `do_split` (`leaves.py:1132-1135`) branches on `cfg.splitter.mode == "command"` and
    falls through to `_stub_split` for **any other mode** — silently. No warning on stderr,
    same rc 0, same printed proposal path. The operator's only signal that no model ran is
    reading the proposal and recognising the fixture.
  - `_stub_split` (`leaves.py:1143-1169`) writes a proposal that is byte-identical in shape
    to a real one. `<!-- pdca:split-proposal v1 -->` is the same header a command-mode
    splitter emits, so nothing on disk records the provenance.
  - `can_file` (`split.py:524-540`) checks only that the tracker is GitHub, the repo
    resolves, and `gh` is on PATH. Its docstring — "Never a silent skip" — is about the
    *opposite* failure; nothing asks whether the proposal is fit to file.
  - `accept` (`split.py:386-404`) runs `parse` + `validate`, which enforce label shape,
    id count, sibling references and cycles. All structural. The stub passes every one,
    because it was written to.
  - `child_title` (`split.py:551-577`) falls back to the child's slug, so the fixture slug
    becomes the tracker issue title verbatim.

  This is the same code path #358 specifies as the **offline** end-to-end test ("stub
  splitter → accept → `pdca flow` over the children"). Offline it is harmless only because
  `can_file` fails or `--ids` is supplied. In a live checkout with `gh` working and no
  `--ids`, the fixture reaches the tracker — and tracker issues cannot be rolled back, which
  is precisely the irreversibility #459 is written around.

  Secondary, and part of why the blast radius is larger than two junk issues: the stub's
  children read as fully planned. `state()` (`state.py:167-187`) calls a bundle `PLANNED`
  once `brief.md` exists with a slug that is neither empty nor `<…>`-wrapped, and
  `is_placeholder` (`brief.py:167-184`) only recognises the unfilled-template shape.
  `stub-child-one` is well-formed kebab-case, so the guard that exists for exactly this
  class of mistake does not fire.

- **Success criterion:**

  (a) A stub-produced `split-proposal.md` is **self-identifying on disk** — a marker in the
      proposal header written by `_stub_split`, not a slug-name sniff and not an in-memory
      flag. `accept` runs in a separate process from `do_split`, so provenance has to
      survive the file.

  (b) `pdca split <id> --accept` **refuses** on a stub-marked proposal, before `can_file`
      and before any `gh issue create`, naming the cause and the fix
      (`[leaves.splitter] mode = "command"`). The refusal is on the *filing*, not on
      acceptance as such.

  (c) `--ids` still accepts a stub-marked proposal, so #358's offline round-trip test keeps
      working unchanged. That path files nothing; the ids already exist and the operator
      supplied them deliberately. This is the seam that separates "exercising the machinery"
      from "reaching the tracker".

  (d) `pdca split <id>` in stub mode says so on **stderr** at the moment it runs, rather than
      leaving the operator to infer it from the proposal's contents. Today's output is
      indistinguishable from a real splitter's.

  (e) Regression test: with `mode = "stub"` and `can_file` returning `(True, repo)`,
      `pdca split <id> --accept` creates no bundles and invokes no `gh issue create`. Assert
      on the absence of the call, not just on the exit code — a refusal that still filed the
      first child before erroring is the failure mode worth locking.

- **Test file:** tests/test_split_stub_guard.py

- **Difficulty:** low

## Deliberately not in scope

**Whether a split child should route through Plan at all.** Today `split.py`'s module
docstring calls each child body "a full draft brief" and `pdca.toml` documents the run
continuing "into waves by itself (#358)" — i.e. straight to Do. With a real splitter that is
a defensible design, and changing it means a new state distinguishing "split seed" from
"planned brief". Worth deciding, separately; this issue is only that a **stub** must not
reach the tracker.

**Retroactive cleanup** of `getwyrd/wyrd#708` / `#709`. Instance data, handled by hand.

## Notes

Related to #459 (convergence reported before `--accept` files irreversible issues) — same
irreversibility, different question. #459 asks whether a *real* split converged; this asks
whether the proposal came from a model at all. A fix for #459 does not catch this: the stub's
two children would likely report as converged.
title: stub splitter mode files its fixture children as real tracker issues — `--accept` cannot tell a placeholder proposal from a real one
